questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x=2\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(2\sqrt{x})-\int (2\sqrt{x})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-4\sqrt{x}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot {x}^{2}-\int {x}^{2}(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-2\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-{x}^{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(3x)\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(3x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(x){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-{\int }_{1}^{e}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e-x{|}_{1}^{e}\,] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}(e-e+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
At first, it may not look like we have two factors. Actually, we do, but one of them is implicit. The trick is to write the integral as

$$
\int \ln{x}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln{x} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x.
$$

 

Using this trick, we can now use integration by parts. We let

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the by-parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
